# emss

## Overview

This package aims to support Embedded Standard Setting, calculating
counts and weights.

## Install

``` r
devtools::install_github("sooyongl/emss", dependencies = T)
```

## Usage

``` r
library(emss)
```

``` r
fake_data <- genFakeDataSet(ngca = 3, 
               cor_val = 0.2,
               n = 30,
               nlevel = 3,
               ntable = 5,
               npanelist = 5,
               sdinp = 1,
               ecinp = 0,
               100,300)



fake_data

# Or you can use your own data structured by the following table.
```

``` r
res <- emstans(data = fake_data,
               grades = c(1, 2),
               location = "Loc_RP50",
               method = "weight",
               smooth = FALSE)
```

## Summary

``` r
summary(res)
#>     unit cut_level modal median average agreement weighted_kappa
#> 1 M1-All    Level2 103.1  118.2  126.22     0.633          0.337
#> 2 M1-All    Level3 283.4  203.7  222.21     0.633          0.337
#> 3 M2-All    Level2 155.7  180.9  194.66     0.633          0.321
#> 4 M2-All    Level3 313.5  300.9  299.17     0.633          0.321
```

## Report

With `what = "all"`, the combined report is provided.

### Individual

``` r
report(res, what = "individual")
```

### Detailed

``` r
report(res, what = "detailed")
```

### Summary

``` r
report(res, what = "summary")
```

### Item Review

``` r
report(res, what = "review")
```

## Extract

[`extract()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/extract.ESS.md)
provides the primary results of ESS as a form of
[`list()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html).

``` r
extract(res)
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`bootstrapping()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/bootstrapping.ESS.md)
  : Bootstrap the modal cut scores of one unit
- [`emstans()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/emstans.md) :
  Run Embedded Standard Setting Analysis
- [`ess_data()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/ess_data.md)
  : Prepare Embedded Standard Setting input data
- [`ess_locations()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/ess_locations.md)
  : Item locations at a response probability
- [`ess_read_excel()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/ess_read_excel.md)
  : Read an emss Excel workbook
- [`extract()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/extract.ESS.md)
  : Extract tables from an ESS result
- [`generateMockDataSet()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/generateMockDataSet.md)
  : Generate a Fake Data Set for Embedded Standard Setting
- [`plot(`*`<ESS>`*`)`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/plot.ESS.md)
  : Plot an ESS result
- [`report()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/report.ESS.md)
  : HTML report of an ESS result
- [`summary(`*`<ESS>`*`)`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/summary.ESS.md)
  : Summarise an ESS result
- [`update(`*`<ESS>`*`)`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/update.ESS.md)
  : Set cut scores manually
- [`validateData()`](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/reference/validateData.md)
  : Check input data

# Articles

### Articles

- [Getting started with
  emss](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/articles/getting-started.md):

  Install emss, prepare the inputs, estimate cut scores and read the
  results.

- [How embedded standard setting
  works](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/articles/ess-method.md):

  The ESS-Count and ESS-Weight criteria worked by hand on a 12-item
  example, with the mathematics behind every result emss reports.

- [Setting cut scores
  manually](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/articles/manual-cut-scores.md):

  Replace estimated cut scores with your own, and see how much
  consistency and impact change.

- [Bootstrapping cut
  scores](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/articles/bootstrapping.md):

  How much would the cut scores change with a different set of items?
  The item bootstrap, how to read it, and the earlier jittered-grid
  version.

- [Item
  locations](https://sooyongl.github.io/emss/articles/item-locations.md):

  What an item location is, why it drives ESS cut scores, how it is
  computed, and what to consider under each IRT model. Covers
  ess_locations().
